catalog_quote: ... stress falls on the penultimate mora of the Kawaiisu word: thus most words are stressed on the penultimate syllable, but words with final long vowels have final stress. However, all vowel-initial pronominal clitics (written here with a = separating them from the preceding word), even disyllabic ones, are treated as single moras for the purposes of the stress rule: (1a) kaʔapi=ni food-my ... 'my food' (1b) kaʔapi=ana food-his ... 'his food' ...

sources.quote: 'In an utterance between junctures every even numbered mora unit preceding the final juncture receives stress. Penultimate mora units receive primary stress and high pitch. The first stressed mora unit after an initial juncture receives a medium high pitch. A vowel cluster counts as two mora units.' (A marginal note adds that the description must be modified for utterances of the form /CVCVCVVCV/.) Klein's sec. 5 'Differences' disputes ZBM only on segmental points (g/gw as stops, -mb-/-bb-, -hm-), not on stress.

sources.note: Independent primary field description (1958-59) stating primary stress on the penultimate mora plus alternating secondary stress on even-numbered morae from the right edge; identifies the 'unattributed AAA abstract' in our the secondary-stress rule field as Klein's and supplies a citable secondary-stress statement.

sources.quote: Abstract: 'I also find that an increase in pitch is the most robust acoustic cue to Kawaiisu stress, and that unstressed vowels often lie more toward the periphery of the vowel space than stressed vowels.' The abstract says the dissertation 'expands on the description of Kawaiisu phonetics and phonology contained in Zigmond et al. (1990), finding support for many of the claims made in their grammar'; it does not state the stress-placement rule.
sources.note: Only acoustic study of Kawaiisu; abstract reports pitch as the main stress cue and tests ZBM's phonological claims against Klein's 1958/1980s recordings -- would give an instrumental check of the penultimate-mora rule and possibly secondary stress, which our record leaves uncoded.
